newsitem.title: UK: Berisford worth over 300 mln stg - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Berisford worth over 300 mln stg - analysts.

text.p: Consumer food products to agri-business company Berisford Plc would attract a price tag of 175 to 200 pence a share, valuing the company at 300 to 365 million stg, if a bid offer is launched, said analysts.
One sector analyst at a British broker said, "At today's earnings, I would see a price of around 200 pence a share."
Berisford's share price soared 23p in the morning session to 145-1/2p, 19 percent higher, after the company said it had received a "formal interest" in an offer.
Another analyst at a Dutch broker said a "logical price" would be anything between 175 and 200 pence per share.
Analysts, who met Berisford management at a meeting called by the company to outline its full year results, said executives were tightlipped over the name of a potential buyer.
However, they said the company confirmed there was just one potential bidder at present.
Swedish consumer goods manufacturer Electrolux was hotly tipped by analysts as the suitor given its estimated cash reserves of more than 600 million stg.
The prize jewel in the company's crown is its U.S. subsidiary Welbilt Corporation which accounts for nearly 60 percent of the company's turnover.
"That makes Electrolux a strong contender, given its presence in the U.S.," said one analyst.
British diversified groups Tomkins Plc and Wassal Plc were also mentioned as possible bidders.
Analysts said Electrolux was more likely to make an outright cash purchase, if it launched an offer, while the British firms would probably favour offering shares.
Berisford earlier reported a slight dip in its pretax profit for the year ending September 28, 1996 to 25.5 million stg from 26.8 million previously.

But its turnover was higher at 497.5 million pounds up from 381.2 in the previous year. The company reported earnings per share of 12.5 pence and offered a total dividend of 4.5 pence per share, against last year's 3.0p.
It also said its sales and orders for the first seven weeks of the current financial year were higher compared to its performance in the previous year.
Berisford said its sales at Magnet were up 11 percent with retail kitchen orders 19 perecnt higher and kitchen sales despatched from its Darlington factory in north east England rose eight percent.
The company said in its results statement that the approach "had been only of a preliminary nature such that it is unclear whether it may or may not lead to an offer being made".
